disclaimers: Rates are for most elections; Primary/Primary Runoff Election Day workers assigned through political parties may be paid different party-set rates
disclosure_of_risks: Election Day is at least a 12-hour day; Early Voting period typically 12 days
guarantees_or_promises: none - hourly county election-worker wage schedule
objective_evidence: County Elections Office published pay schedule

standard.s3: Hourly pay for most elections: Presiding Judge $17/hour; Presiding Alternate Judge $16/hour; Election Clerks $15/hour. Presiding Judge and Alternate Judge receive an additional $25 payment for delivery of election supplies to the Elections Office.
standard.s4: Must be a registered voter of Collin County (or the political subdivision conducting the election); training required. Primary/Runoff party-assigned workers may face separate party paperwork and rates.
standard.s5: Official: Election Day typically at least a 12-hour day. Early Voting period for a Texas election typically lasts 12 days.
standard.s6: Election Day minimum ~12 hours per county statement; typical Texas polling-day length 13-15 hours with setup/close.
